call_points.text: Net VNB margin rose to 22.9% in Q1FY27 from 15.4% a year earlier, a 7.5-point gain.
Overall expense ratio rose 16 bps to 10.63% and commission ratio fell 20 bps to 3.95%.
call_points.versus_prior: FY26 expense ratio was 11.91% on the last call

call_points.text: Bancassurance and alternate channels sold 44,752 individual policies, up 16.35% from 38,462.
Yield on policyholders' fund fell 17 bps to 8.28%; yield on shareholders' fund rose 7 bps to 6.21%.
Total gross NPA ratio improved to 1.21% from 1.42%.
Solvency ratio strengthened to 2.35 as of March 31, 2026, from 2.11 a year earlier.
Dividend payout policy stays cautious until risk-based capital rules are clear; the board recommended ₹10 per share, ₹20 pre-bonus.
Overall expense ratio fell 51 bps to 11.91% in FY26, which management called the lowest since listing.
Bancassurance and alternate channels crossed ₹5,000 Cr for the first time, collecting ₹5,076 Cr of new business premium, up 45.19%.
61st-month persistency fell to 59.31% on premium basis from 63.12%; management cited COVID-era product mix and expects improvement across cohorts.
Individual agents fell to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851; management said recruitment and productivity are the focus.
Management said risk-based capital could raise capital needs given LIC's equity exposure, and declined to quantify the impact.
April 2026 performance was better than the prior year across participating and non-participating business, though management said it is too early to comment on market volatility.
No numeric FY27 targets are given; the way forward lists seven focus areas including digital transformation and consolidating the non-par share.

operating_notes.text: Individual non-par APE grew to ₹15,214 Cr in FY26.
LIC's New Jeevan Sathi – Single Premium and Limited Premium are non-par, non-linked, individual savings plans sold in the domestic market from June 1, 2026.
FY26 individual non-par APE was ₹15,214 Cr, 35.11% of individual APE versus 27.69% in FY25.
FY26 IEV of ₹7,89,185 Cr comprised adjusted net worth of ₹1,69,605 Cr and value of in-force of ₹6,19,580 Cr.
FY26 61st-month persistency was 63.12% on premium basis and 50.31% on policy-count basis.
FY26 individual non-par APE reached ₹15,214 Cr, 35.11% of individual APE, versus 27.69% in FY25.
FY26 VNB margin walk: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes including GST -2.8%.
FY26 AUM was ₹57,29,396 Cr, up 5.08% YoY, and IEV was ₹7,89,185 Cr, up 1.58%.
FY2022-23 reverse-charge input-tax credit dispute: GST of ₹9.91 Cr, penalty of ₹9.91 Cr and interest as applicable.

Uttar Pradesh GST demand for FY2018-19 to FY2020-21: GST of ₹95.24 Cr, penalty of ₹95.24 Cr and interest as applicable, over excess ITC claimed and short tax paid; appeal to be filed before the GST Appellate Tribunal.
OFS base offer of 31,62,49,885 shares (2.50%) with an oversubscription option of 50,59,99,816 shares (4.00%), floor price ₹382, retail/employee discount ₹10.
Q1FY27 net VNB was ₹3,136 Cr on total APE of ₹13,692 Cr, a VNB margin of 22.9% against 15.4% in Q1FY26.
Non-par products were 32.49% of individual APE in Q1FY27, up from 30.34% a year earlier.
Indian Embedded Value was ₹7,89,185 Cr at March 2026, up 1.58% from ₹7,76,876 Cr at March 2025.
LIC's New Bima Jyoti, a non-par, non-linked, individual savings plan, is available for sale from 10 August 2026 in the domestic market.
The promoter proposed an OFS of up to 2.50% of paid-up capital as the Base Offer Size, with an option to additionally sell 4.00%, plus an employee offer of up to 50,00,000 shares.
Q1FY27 segment VNB margins: par 19.4%, individual non-par 49.3% and group 29.4%, on APE proportions of 37.1%, ₹1,678 crore and 45% respectively.
Funds for available solvency margin (ASM) stood at ₹180,000 crore at book value as of the Q1FY27 call.
The minimum sum assured on major selling products was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh, which management said lifted average ticket size and margins.
Subscribed to 500,000 NCDs of Bajaj Finance Limited worth ₹5,000 crore.
Two new non-par, non-linked individual plans, Bima Platinum (savings) and Jeevan Raksha (pure risk), to be sold from September 7, 2026.
Managing Director and KMP Dinesh Pant ceased to hold office on voluntary retirement approved by the Government of India; he also ceased to chair the Information Technology Strategy Committee.
Chief Financial Officer and KMP Shatmanyu Shrivastava superannuated after close of office hours; no successor named in the filing.
LIC to launch three non-par, non-linked individual products from October 19, 2026 — New Jeevan Dhara - II (deferred annuity, savings), Health Shield and New Cancer Cover (both pure-risk health).

timeline.summary: Life Insurance Corporation of India approved issue of bonus shares (99.9998% in favor) via postal ballot on May 17, 2026.
LIC reported FY26 PAT of ₹57,419 Cr (+19.25% YoY) with a VNB margin of 21.2% and recommended a final dividend of ₹10 per share.
LIC reported FY26 standalone PAT of ₹57,419 Cr and VNB margin of 21.2%.
LIC said it will launch two non-par, non-linked individual savings plans, New Jeevan Sathi – Single Premium and Limited Premium, for sale from June 1, 2026.
LIC's FY26 corporate presentation (May 22, 2026) showed VNB margin rising to 21.2% from 17.6% on 43.78% growth in individual non-par APE, with IEV up 1.58% to ₹7,89,185 Cr and solvency at 2.35.
Life Insurance Corporation of India (LICI) will participate in an institutional investor meet on May 29, 2026, organized by 360 ONE (B&K) Securities India Pvt Ltd at Grand Hyatt, Mumbai.
LIC reported FY26 consolidated PAT of ₹57,419 Cr with a VNB margin of 21.2% and recommended a final dividend of ₹10 per share.
On June 1, 2026, LIC allotted 632.50 crore bonus equity shares in a 1:1 ratio, doubling its paid-up capital to ₹1,265 Cr.
LIC held its 5th AGM on July 27, 2026, passing all seven resolutions including financial statement adoption and director appointments.
On 30 July 2026, LIC received a Jharkhand GST demand for FY2022-23, including ₹9.91 Cr GST, ₹9.91 Cr penalty and interest, and said it would appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals), Jamshedpur.

On 31 July 2026, LIC received a GST, interest and penalty demand order from the Commissioner Appeals CGST & Central Excise, Allahabad, for FY2018-19 to FY2020-21, with GST of ₹95.24 Cr and a penalty of ₹95.24 Cr; it said it would appeal to the GST Appellate Tribunal.

On 3 August 2026, the President of India, LIC's promoter, announced an offer for sale of up to 31,62,49,885 shares (2.50%) at a ₹382 floor price on August 4-5, with an oversubscription option of a further 50,59,99,816 shares (4%).
On August 4, 2026, Government of India exercised oversubscription option for 50,59,99,816 equity shares in LIC's Offer for Sale, increasing total offer size to 82,22,49,701 shares (6.5% stake)
On 6 August 2026, LIC's Q1FY27 investor presentation showed net VNB up 61.32% to ₹3,136 Cr, VNB margin at 22.9% from 15.4%, PAT up 22.81% to ₹13,492 Cr and solvency at 2.42.
Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) will participate in an investor meet with Emkay Global Financial Group on August 13, 2026, at Grand Hyatt Mumbai.
On 7 August 2026, LIC said it will launch LIC's New Bima Jyoti, a non-par, non-linked individual savings plan, for sale from 10 August 2026.
LIC announced a promoter Offer for Sale by the President of India of up to equity with greenshoe option.
LIC reported Q1FY27 PAT of ₹13,492 Cr with a VNB margin of 22.9% and announced a 6.5% promoter OFS.
Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) will present at Motilal Oswal’s 22nd Annual Global Investor Conference on August 17, 2026, at Hyatt Mumbai.
LIC subscribed to ₹5,000 crore of Non-Convertible Debentures issued by Bajaj Finance Limited.
LIC said it will launch two non-par, non-linked individual plans, Bima Platinum (savings) and Jeevan Raksha (pure risk), for sale from September 7, 2026.
Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) will participate in one-on-one meetings with Group and Jefferies on September 18, 2026, at The Oberoi, Gurgaon.
LIC received a stock exchange clarification query under Regulation 33 concerning its Q1FY27 financial results.
LIC said the Government of India approved the voluntary retirement of Managing Director and KMP Dinesh Pant, effective September 24, 2026.
LIC Chief Financial Officer Shatmanyu Shrivastava superannuated on September 30, 2026.
LIC said it will launch three non-par, non-linked products — New Jeevan Dhara - II annuity, Health Shield and New Cancer Cover — for sale from October 19, 2026.
